newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision holds top spot for Garden stake.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision holds top spot for Garden stake.

text.p: Cablevision Systems Corp has secured the upper hand to buy ITT Corp's 50 percent stake in world-famous Madison Square Garden, although several major media companies also have lined up to bid.
Sources close to the situation said Thursday that ITT and Cablevision, which each own 50 percent of the properties, have quietly resolved a dispute over ownership rights to it.
The two companies have agreed that while Cablevision is not entitled to prevent another company from bidding, it has the right to compete with the best bid, they said.
The sources, which did not want to be identified, said it was not immediately clear if Cablevision would have to match the bid or exceed it.
One source said he believed Cablevision would only have to top a competing offer by $1.
A spokesman for ITT declined to comment. A Cablevision spokesman could not be reached for comment.
Although no formal bids have been submitted, interest has been expressed by News Corp Ltd, General Electric Co, Westinghouse Electric Corp, Walt Disney Co and Loews Corp, the sources said.
Westinghouse, Loews, General Electric and Disney also declined to comment.
A spokesman for News Corp declined to discuss Madison Square Garden specifically, but noted that the company has said it would consider any available media property.
Cablevision last week said it would be interested in buying ITT's stake.

The sale of ITT's stake in Madison Square Garden is expected to be the next critcal step for the hotel, casino and entertainment company as it tries to defend itself against a $6.5 billion hostile takeover by Hilton Hotels Corp.
Part of ITT's defense against Hilton is expected to be the sale of non-core assets. The company has said it would consider selling the assets in order to focus on the hotel and casino businesses.

ITT partnered with Cablevision in 1995 to buy the Madison Square Garden properties, which include the world-famous arena, the New York Knicks professional basketball team and the New York Rangers professional hockey team.
A dispute arose earlier this month when Cablevision contended that it had right of first refusal for ITT's 50 percent stake. ITT disputed that claim.
ITT declined to comment. A spokesman for Cablevision could not be reached for comment.
The sources said ITT is in the process of soliciting bids from interested companies, although they stressed that the process is still relatively informal at this point.

They also said that ITT would prefer a sale to Cablevision versus any other bidder because Cablevision is already so familiar with the properties that it would not require due diligence, enabling rapid closure of the deal.
